correctness.rationale: A blue edge in the underlying complete bipartite graph has white-neighbor count equal to the sum of the white degrees of its endpoints; any force therefore deletes a white edge at a degree-one vertex using an opposite-side isolate. A cycle cannot lose its first edge. Two isolates on opposite sides persist and allow every successive forest leaf to be peeled. With an isolate on just one side, the required opposite-side leaf permits the first deletion, which creates the second isolate. An empty white graph is accepted. In the tree EGF, degree minus one is the occurrence count in the relevant bipartite Prüfer word. Expanding a factor 1+(t−1) for each absent label gives Q. Among forests the rejection condition is the union of three events: no isolates on either side, no right isolates or right leaves, and no left isolates or left leaves. Inclusion–exclusion gives precisely the six signs because the intersection of the latter two is contained in the first. Maximum white edge count m+n−2 requires components consisting of one isolate and one tree; a tree with the required leaf exists, e.g. a bipartite double star, including when one part has size one. Removing the surjective words on the side requiring a leaf gives the stated minimum count. Direct simulation independently matched every one of 4,688 subsets on 2×2, 2×3, 3×3 and 3×4; the minimum counts were 4, 14, 72 and 420. The same classification, all coefficients and extremal witness counts are already available.
